# Monster Battle 9001: Voice Lines

<!-- Generated by tools/audio/voice/build.sh (mbvoice/docgen.py). Edit that, not this file. -->

Every spoken line in the game as a finished sound file: **162 lines, 5 voices, 410 seconds of audio**, each as `.ogg` (Vorbis, quality 3) and `.mp3` (quality 5), 3.1 MB and 3.2 MB in all. The words are in `docs/VOICE_SCRIPT.md`; this page is about how they are spoken, processed and checked.

Since round 4 (`docs/ROADMAP.md`) almost every line is one a player chooses: the communication rose's army lines, shouted by the squad leaders over the radio (each squad in its own voice). The only line the game says by itself is the news telling the monster's player that the creature can molt.

- Sound files: `client/public/assets/audio/voice/<lineId>.ogg` and `.mp3`
- Manifest: `client/public/assets/manifest.voice.json` (section `voice`, with each line's length)
- Generator: `tools/audio/voice/` (`build.sh` rebuilds only what changed; `--force` rebuilds everything)
- Measurements behind this page: `docs/audio/voice/measurements.json`; one picture per voice, `docs/audio/voice/sheet_<voice>.png` (unprocessed speech left, finished clip right)

The voices are neural speech models (Kokoro-82M, and Piper for one voice) run on the build machine's processor with no network; the model files are downloaded once into a folder outside the repository. Nobody listened while these were made (the build machine has no speakers): the build checks every file by measurement, and two speech recognizers transcribe every finished clip.

The last build finished with **0 failed checks**.

## 1. The cast

| Voice | Heard by | Who | Speech model | Chain | Pace (words/s) | Lines |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| **Granite** | Everyone (radio) | Squad 1's leader, shouting into the radio. | Kokoro-82M `am_fenrir`, rate 1.15, pitch +1 semitones, 3 exclamation marks | radio | 4.1 | 40 |
| **Beacon** | Everyone (radio) | Squad 2's leader. | Kokoro-82M `af_sky`, rate 1.12, pitch +1.5 semitones, 3 exclamation marks | radio | 3.69 | 40 |
| **Tempest** | Everyone (radio) | Squad 3's leader. | Piper `en_GB-alba-medium`, rate 1.15, 3 exclamation marks | radio | 3.43 | 40 |
| **Anvil** | Everyone (radio) | Squad 4's leader. | Kokoro-82M `am_echo`, rate 1.15, pitch +2 semitones, 3 exclamation marks | radio | 3.48 | 40 |
| **Anchor** | The monster's player | The Channel 9 news anchor: total professional calm. | Kokoro-82M `af_heart`, rate 0.85 | broadcast | 2.95 | 2 |

**Shouting.** The squad leaders are pushed to yell: faster speech, the pitch raised a semitone or two, extra exclamation marks fed to the speech model (the subtitle keeps one), and a hotter radio chain than the default: more compression, more overdrive into the clipper, a narrower band and louder static. ## 2. The checks

Every file is decoded again and measured: loudness -16 LUFS (loudness units relative to full scale) within 0.8, true peak under -0.5 dB (decibels) of full scale (mastered to -1.5), clean edges, radio lines band-limited, a rose line at most 4.5 seconds, and what the two speech recognizers hear: pocketsphinx (old, strict, easily thrown by radio grit) and a modern recognizer. Word errors are the words a recognizer got wrong, per hundred words of the line.

| Voice | Lines | Seconds | Loudness (LUFS) | Highest peak (dB) | Word errors, modern | Word errors, pocketsphinx |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Granite | 40 | 1.7 to 3.4 | -16.2 to -16.0 | -1.4 | 2.9 | 35.9 |
| Beacon | 40 | 2.0 to 3.5 | -16.2 to -16.0 | -1.1 | 1.2 | 34.1 |
| Tempest | 40 | 2.1 to 3.5 | -16.2 to -16.0 | -1.3 | 2.9 | 73.5 |
| Anvil | 40 | 2.1 to 3.5 | -16.2 to -16.0 | -1.6 | 1.5 | 17.6 |
| Anchor | 2 | 3.2 to 3.8 | -16.1 to -16.0 | -1.2 | 0.0 | 10.0 |
| **Everything** | 162 | 1.7 to 3.8 | -16.2 to -16.0 | -1.1 | 2.1 | 39.9 |

## 3. Changing the lines

- Words: `client/src/audio/roseLines.json` (the rose) or `shared/src/defs/voiceLines.json` (the molt line); then `tools/audio/voice/build.sh` and `npm run assets:manifest`. The rules are in `docs/VOICE_SCRIPT.md`.
- A voice: `tools/audio/voice/cast.json`. A different speech service: replace `synthesize` in `tools/audio/voice/mbvoice/synth.py`; everything after it (radio chain, loudness, files, checks) stays.
- Respellings fed to the speech model (the subtitle never changes): `tools/audio/voice/pronounce.json`.
